newsitem.title: UK: Pilkington Q1 Euro trade remains difficult.
newsitem.headline: Pilkington Q1 Euro trade remains difficult.

text.p: British glass and plastic products manufacturer Pilkington Plc said on Thursday the difficult European trading conditions seen in the second half of last year have continued into the first quarter this year.
The company told shareholders at its annual general meeting glass prices had increased from their low point at the end of March but remained "relatively subdued".

The group said a major restructuring programme is underway in its European automotive glazing business, which will involve closing one of its two large German plants and the reduction in its European workforce by 20 percent -- over 1,000 people.

Pilkington also said it would have a thorough review of its building products business in Europe where profits had been "totally inadequate". This was expected to lead to significant rationalisation, particularly in the UK and in Germany.
The group also hoped to make a significant reduction in overhead costs, which it said totalled 1.0 billion pounds ($1.7 billion), or 30 percent of turnover.
These actions will result in further rationalisation costs and asset write-offs in the current financial year.

"It is too early to be precise in terms of numbers, but the pay back on these programmes is quick and we should be through the major cost impact before March 1998, with the benefits increasingly underpinning the future competitiveness of the group," the company said in a statement.
